newsitem.title: FRANCE: French projections show combined left ahead.
newsitem.headline: French projections show combined left ahead.

text.p: The combined left showed a strong lead over the ruling centre-right coalition in the first round of France's parliamentary election on Sunday, all polling institutes said.

In projections broadcast as soon as polling stations closed at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT), polling institute BVA gave the Socialist party 29 percent of the vote, the Communist party 9.6 percent, the ruling RPR-UDF coalition 37.2 percent and the National Front 14.8 percent.
The Sofres institute gave the Socialist party 27 percent of the vote, the Communist party 9.5 percent, the ruling RPR-UDF coalition 31.5 percent and the National Front 15.3 percent.

The CSA institute gave the total left 40.7 percent, including 27.3 percent for the Socialist party and 9.8 percent for the Communist party. It gave the ruling RPR-UDF coalition 36.7 percent and the National Front 14.9 percent.
